art.public_api:
## Primitives (scripts/world/primitives.gd). All old signatures still work; material() now returns a cached toon ShaderMaterial.
- static material(color: Color, emission: float = 0.0, unshaded: bool = false, outline: bool = true) -> ShaderMaterial
  - Delegates to ArtKit.toon_material. If alpha < 1 the material is see-through (toon_alpha / toon_unshaded_alpha shader) and gets no outline.
  - Set outline=false for walls, floors and decals.
- static material_color(mat: Material) -> Color
  - Reads "albedo" from a ShaderMaterial or albedo_color from a BaseMaterial3D. Returns Color(0,0,0,0) for anything else.
  - Use this instead of `(mat as StandardMaterial3D).albedo_color`.
- static box(size: Vector3, color: Color, emission := 0.0, radius := 0.0) -> MeshInstance3D
  - radius = 0: a BoxMesh with mesh.material set, as before.
  - radius > 0: a MeshFactory.rounded_box via material_override.
- static cylinder(radius, height, color, sides := 10, top_radius := -1.0) -> MeshInstance3D (unchanged)
- static rounded_cylinder(radius: float, height: float, color: Color, bevel := 0.02, sides := 24, emission := 0.0) -> MeshInstance3D
- static sphere(radius, color, segments := 8, emission := 0.0) -> MeshInstance3D (unchanged)
- static capsule(radius, height, color) -> MeshInstance3D (unchanged; now 12 radial segments, 3 rings)
- static pill(length: float, radius: float, color: Color, emission := 0.0) -> MeshInstance3D (capsule along X)
- static prism(size, color) -> MeshInstance3D (unchanged)
- static mesh_instance(mesh: Mesh, color: Color, emission := 0.0, outline := true) -> MeshInstance3D
  - Toon material_override, plus the mesh's outline mode.
- static label(text, pixel_size := 0.01, color := WHITE, billboard := true) -> Label3D
  - Lilita One at font_size 48, outline_size 13 in #1c0f2e.
- static static_box(size, color, layer := 1, radius := 0.0) -> StaticBody3D

## ArtKit (scripts/world/art/art_kit.gd, static)
Consts:
- SHADER_TOON, SHADER_TOON_ALPHA, SHADER_TOON_UNSHADED, SHADER_TOON_UNSHADED_ALPHA, SHADER_OUTLINE, SHADER_CARPET, SHADER_WALL, SHADER_FELT, SHADER_SCREEN, SHADER_NEON
- OUTLINE_COLOR = #1c0f2e
- OUTLINE_WIDTH = 2.6 (px at 900p)
- HOVER_COLOR = #fff06a
- DISPLAY_FONT_PATH, BODY_FONT_PATH

Materials (all cached by parameters and shared — never mutate them):
- toon_material(color, emission := 0.0, unshaded := false, outline := true, gloss := 0.0, vertex_color := false) -> ShaderMaterial
  - gloss is a toon specular highlight; about 0.5 gives glossy keys.
- outline_material(color := OUTLINE_COLOR, width := OUTLINE_WIDTH) -> ShaderMaterial
- carpet_material(colors: Array (base, c1, c2, c3), pattern := ArtPalette.CARPET_EYES, tile := 1.3) -> ShaderMaterial
- carpet_for(palette, tile := 1.3) -> ShaderMaterial
- wall_material(base, alt, line, pattern := WALL_DIAMONDS, tile := 0.9, line_glow := 0.0, rail_height := 1.1) -> ShaderMaterial
- wall_for(palette) -> ShaderMaterial
- ceiling_for(palette, line_glow := 0.4, tile := 1.6) -> ShaderMaterial
- felt_material(color, border := #ffe08a, half_size := Vector2(0.5,0.5), corner_radius := 0.12, shape := 0 (0 rounded rect, 1 ellipse)) -> ShaderMaterial
  - Uses object-space XZ, so half_size is the felt's half extents in metres.
- screen_material(color := #0b0614, glow := #8c4dff, brightness := 1.0) -> ShaderMaterial
  - Needs 0..1 UVs: a QuadMesh or a face of rounded_box.
  - Put Label3D text just in front of it.
  - The shader also has use_texture / screen_texture for a SubViewport.
- neon_material(color, energy := 2.0, pulse_speed := 0.0) -> ShaderMaterial (unshaded, HDR so it blooms, no outline)
- material_cache_size() -> int

Instances and per-object tweaks (instance uniforms, no material duplication):
- mesh_instance(mesh: Mesh, material: Material) -> MeshInstance3D
- outline_mode_for(mesh) -> int
- set_outline_mode(gi: GeometryInstance3D, mode: int)
- set_outline_hover(root: Node, on: bool, color := HOVER_COLOR)
  - Recurses over every MeshInstance3D / MultiMeshInstance3D under root.
  - Thick (6 px), pulsing, glowing outline, plus a slight body lift.
- is_outline_hovered(root) -> bool
- set_neon_level(gi, level: float)
  - Dims or brightens a neon mesh (0..1) for chasing bulbs.

Palette and environment:
- palette_for(casino: Dictionary) -> Dictionary (delegates to ArtPalette.for_casino)
- make_environment(palette: Dictionary, fog := true) -> Environment
  - Glow on: screen blend, threshold 1.25 (Forward+) / 1.3 (compat), so only neon, emissive bits and hover outlines bloom.
  - Filmic tonemap, white point 2.0.
  - Ambient colour from palette.ambient at palette.ambient_energy (0.6 default).
  - Saturation 1.1, contrast 1.05.
  - Exponential fog: 0.012, or 0.006 for day casinos.
  - Pre-linearises the background colour on compat.
- make_world_environment(palette, fog := true) -> WorldEnvironment (named "Environment")
- make_key_light(palette, energy := 0.7) -> DirectionalLight3D (named "KeyLight", shadows on)
- neon_light(color, energy := 1.0, light_range := 6.0) -> OmniLight3D

Fonts and labels:
- display_font() -> Font (Lilita One)
- body_font(weight := 600) -> FontVariation (Fredoka, wght axis)
- make_label(text, pixel_size := 0.01, color := WHITE, font_size := 48, billboard := true) -> Label3D (display font, thick dark outline)
- floating_sign(text, size := 0.45, color := WHITE) -> FloatingSign

## FloatingSign extends Label3D (scripts/world/art/floating_sign.gd)
- const SIGN_FONT_SIZE = 128
- @export fade_start := 9.0, fade_end := 16.0 (metres from the active camera), bob_pixels := 6.0, bob_speed := 1.7
- var base_color
- setup(text, size_m, color)
- fade_alpha() -> float
- Billboarded. _process bobs it via `offset` and fades modulate and outline alpha.

## MeshFactory (scripts/world/art/mesh_factory.gd, static)
Every mesh is cached and shared, so never set a material on one; colour each instance with material_override.
Consts:
- META_OUTLINE_MODE = &"outline_mode"
- OUTLINE_SMOOTH = 0, OUTLINE_BOX = 1, OUTLINE_CYLINDER = 2

Functions:
- rounded_box(size: Vector3, radius := 0.05, segments := 3) -> ArrayMesh
  - Smooth normals, 0..1 UVs per face (+Z face: u left→right, v top→bottom).
  - 6*(2s+2)^2 vertices; radius 0 gives a 24-vertex box.
- pill(length, radius, segments := 4) -> ArrayMesh (along X)
- ball(radius, segments := 4) -> ArrayMesh
- capsule(radius, height, radial := 16, rings := 6) -> CapsuleMesh
- rounded_cylinder(radius, height, bevel := 0.02, sides := 24, bevel_segments := 3) -> ArrayMesh
- lathe(points: PackedVector2Array (radius, y) bottom→top, sides := 24, smooth := true) -> ArrayMesh
- blob(height, bottom_radius, top_radius, sides := 24, rings := 14) -> ArrayMesh
  - Bean or pear body from y = 0 to height.
- torus(inner_radius, outer_radius, rings := 32, ring_segments := 12) -> TorusMesh
- quad(size: Vector2) -> QuadMesh
- wedge(size: Vector3, front_ratio := 0.35, bevel := 0.0) -> ArrayMesh
  - Sloped console: tall at -Z, low at +Z.
- extrude(polygon: PackedVector2Array, depth, bevel := 0.0) -> ArrayMesh (XY polygon, centred on z = 0)
- stroke(points, width, depth := 0.03, closed := true) -> ArrayMesh (neon tube tracing a shape)
- star(outer, inner, points := 5, depth := 0.04, stroke_width := 0.0) -> ArrayMesh
- bolt(height, depth := 0.04, stroke_width := 0.0) -> ArrayMesh
- triangle(size, depth := 0.04, stroke_width := 0.0) -> ArrayMesh
- star_points(...), bolt_points(height), triangle_points(size) -> PackedVector2Array
- clear_cache(), cache_size()

## ArtPalette (scripts/world/art/art_palette.gd)
- for_casino(casino: Dictionary) -> Dictionary
  - Colour keys: wall, wall_alt, wall_dark, wall_line, ceiling, floor_a (carpet base), floor_b, floor_c, floor_d, neon_1..neon_4, felt, felt_border, wood, wood_dark, metal, gold, red, text, outline, ambient, fog, sky.
  - Floats: ambient_energy, wall_glow, wall_tile.
  - Ints: carpet_pattern, wall_pattern.
  - Bool: day.
- club() -> Dictionary
- push(c, min_sat, min_val, max_val) -> Color
- carpet_colors(palette) -> Array[Color]
- neons(palette) -> Array[Color]
- Consts:
  - CLUB_WALL, CLUB_WALL_DEEP, CLUB_CEILING
  - NEON_MAGENTA/CYAN/LIME/SUNFLOWER/ORANGE, NEONS, FELT_GREEN, CASINO_RED, GOLD, OUTLINE, TEXT
  - CARPET_EYES = 0, CARPET_STARS = 1, CARPET_CONFETTI = 2
  - WALL_DIAMONDS = 0, WALL_SQUARES = 1, WALL_ZIGZAG = 2, WALL_STRIPES = 3
  - OVERRIDES: hand-tuned entries per casino id

## Shader instance uniforms (shared by name across the toon and outline passes)
- outline_hover (float 0..1)
- outline_hover_color (vec4)
- outline_mode (float: 0 normals, 1 per-axis box, 2 radial-XZ cylinder)
- neon_level (float, neon shader)

## UiTheme
Public API unchanged.
- bold_font() -> FontVariation: Fredoka at weight 600.
- heavy_font() -> FontVariation: base font Lilita One.
art.summary:
I built the toon art kit and checked every piece visually under Xvfb with opengl3, comparing against ref1–ref8. Showcase renders of all six casinos, a kit sheet and a first-person bet console all match the references' vibe without copying them.

**Toon shading and outline**
- One shared include drives all lit surfaces: three cel bands with soft edges, Godot-correct light energy, an optional toon highlight and a fresnel rim. It comes in four variants (opaque, alpha, unshaded, unshaded alpha), plus a top fill and a hover lift.
- The outline is an inverted hull, 2.6 px at 900p, thinning with distance, in #1c0f2e. Hard-edged meshes (BoxMesh, PrismMesh, CylinderMesh and extrusions) get a per-axis or radial grow mode so their corners don't tear; Primitives and ArtKit set this automatically.
- Hover uses per-instance shader uniforms, so it never duplicates materials. It gives a thick, pulsing, glowing yellow outline, and the colour can be changed per call.

**Compatibility-renderer findings**
- `PROJECTION_MATRIX[1][1]` reads as 0 inside vertex() on compat, which made the outlines vanish. I measure pixel size by projecting a 1 m step instead.
- `VIEWPORT_SIZE` also fails in vertex() on compat.
- With glow on, compat converts the clear colour to sRGB twice. `make_environment` pre-linearises the background on compat.
- Compat HDR tops out near 2.0.
- Filmic with white point 1.0 lifted mid-tones about 25%, which washed everything out. I use a white point of 2.0.
- Glow thresholds (1.25 on Forward+, 1.3 on compat) are tuned so only neon, emissive parts and hover outlines bloom. Carpets, lit surfaces and white text do not.

**Materials and environment**
- Pattern shaders tile in world space:
  - Carpet: eyes and swirls, stars and pink cards for the Apex, or confetti. Recoloured per casino and set a little darker than props.
  - Wall panels: diamonds, squares, zigzag or pinstripes, with optional glowing piping and a dado rail.
  - Felt: noise plus an inset border.
  - Screen: dark glass with scanlines and edge glow.
  - Neon: HDR tube with pulse, flicker and a per-instance level.
- `palette_for` pushes each casino's Tuning colours toward the night-club palette, with hand-tuned overrides from the per-casino notes in ART_DIRECTION.md (the Apex is a bright white/gold/sky casino with a starry carpet).
- `make_environment` sets glow, Filmic, palette ambient, a saturation boost and optional fog. There are also key-light and neon omni-light helpers.

**Meshes**
MeshFactory builds rounded boxes, pills, balls, bevelled cylinders, lathes, blobs, wedges, extrusions and neon strokes (star, lightning bolt, triangle), all cached by parameters. One pass in `_commit` winds every triangle to match Godot's convention.

**Labels, signs and fonts**
- Labels use Lilita One with a thick outline.
- FloatingSign is billboarded, bobs gently and fades with distance from the camera.
- UiTheme now uses Fredoka SemiBold for body text and Lilita One for display text.
- Font loading falls back to reading the raw TTF when the import is missing. I hit a flaky headless-import crash once while other processes were running.

**Tests**
`tests/unit/test_art_kit.gd` has 21 tests covering material caching, rounded-mesh validity (vertex counts, normalised normals, outward normals, winding matching BoxMesh), environment glow, palettes for every casino, hover toggling without new materials, outline modes, fonts, the floating-sign fade, and rendering every shader. My tests (test_art_kit plus test_primitives, 23 total) pass with no errors both headless and under the real opengl3 renderer, so shader compilation is genuinely exercised.

**Full suite:** 828 passed, 3 failed. All failures and the 85 'albedo_color on Nil' script errors come from other agents' code that assumes Primitives.material returns a StandardMaterial3D.
needs_from_others: CharacterModel owner: `get_slot_color()` (scripts/world/character_model.gd:311) casts `material_override as StandardMaterial3D`, which is now a toon ShaderMaterial, so it returns null and errors. Replace it with `Primitives.material_color(mi.material_override)`. This one change fixes the 3 failing tests in test_character_model.gd.

test_character_model.gd:250-251 and test_interactable.gd:166-167 cast to StandardMaterial3D. Switch them to `Primitives.material_color(...)`. The test_interactable error doesn't show up as a FAIL, because the script error aborts the test function, but it does trip test.sh.
Builders and machine modules should use `ArtKit.wall_for` / `carpet_for` / `ceiling_for(palette)` for rooms and pass `outline=false` (`Primitives.material(c, e, false, false)`) for walls and floors.
Hover should go through `ArtKit.set_outline_hover(node, true/false)`, not material swaps.
Game-name signs should use `ArtKit.floating_sign`.
Light energies: around 0.6 ambient, a 0.7 key light and 1.0 neon omni lights keep lit surfaces under the glow threshold.
Neon wall art (stroke shapes) belongs on the darker club walls. The Apex walls are cream/gold, so its builder should rely on chandeliers and gold trim rather than neon there.
docs/ARCHITECTURE.md still says the art is graybox with StandardMaterial3D. I don't own that file; the integration stage should document the art kit there (the API is in public_api).
open_issues: Full suite: 828 passed, 3 failed. All 3 failures are in test_character_model.gd, plus script errors from test_interactable.gd:167. They come from StandardMaterial3D casts in other agents' files; see needs_from_others. The leak warnings at exit come from those aborted tests.

Forward+ isn't verifiable here: there's no Vulkan, only llvmpipe GL. The shaders avoid compat-unsafe built-ins and the glow numbers have Forward+ equivalents, but the Forward+ bloom strength and tonemap should get a quick look on real hardware.

Hard-edged meshes rely on the per-instance `outline_mode`. Callers who put Primitives.material on their own BoxMesh/CylinderMesh without going through Primitives or ArtKit.mesh_instance should call `ArtKit.set_outline_mode(mi, ArtKit.outline_mode_for(mesh))`, or they'll see small outline gaps at corners.

Pattern shaders use derivative-based anti-aliasing and fade to an average colour far away. Carpet tiling is world XZ, so carpets only look right on horizontal floors; wall panels choose their projection plane from the surface normal.

The headless `--import` crashed once (signal 11 during the font import) while other godot processes were running; reruns were fine. Fonts fall back to the raw TTF when no .import file exists, so nothing errors.

fp.public_api:
PlayerCharacter (class_name kept, extends CharacterBody3D, scripts/world/player_character.gd). Every previous public method, signal, const and var is kept.
NEW vars: hands: FirstPersonHands (local only, child of camera_rig.camera), id_card: IdCard3D (made on first use), look_pitch: float, reach: float = FpTuning.REACH, net_pitch: float (synced every frame).
KEPT, now first person: camera_rig: CameraRig (local only); facing = the look heading while free (the dive direction mid-dive, the seat/carrier heading otherwise); camera_focus() = eye position per state.
Kept signals: interact_pressed(target: Interactable), interact_held(target: Interactable), tackle_requested(target: Node3D), bumped(guard), throw_chips_requested(position), knock_over_requested(target: Interactable), struggled(), pause_requested(), focus_changed(target: Interactable) (the legacy Interactable focus), stand_requested(), give_chips_requested(target: PlayerCharacter), emoted(emote_id).

- hover_changed(target: Node, hint: String): target is a pressable, an Interactable or null; hint is raw get_hint() / prompt text; re-emitted when the hint text changes.
- primary_pressed(), primary_released(): LMB or E, always, captured or not.
- target_pressed(target: Node), target_held(target: Node)

- capture_changed(capturer: Object)

New methods:

- begin_capture(capturer: Object), end_capture(capturer: Object = null), is_captured() -> bool, capture_owner() -> Object. While captured, LMB/E calls capturer.on_primary_pressed(pid) / on_primary_released(pid) if it has them, and nothing is pressed. Being carried or hidden ends the capture.

- look_toward(point: Vector3), eye_position() -> Vector3, look_direction() -> Vector3
Interaction rules: each physics frame a ray from the camera centre (reach 2.6 m, mask 16, bodies and areas, up to 4 hops) prefers the first pressable (duck typed: has press(); the collider or its parent). A disabled pressable blocks the ray. An enabled Interactable on the ray is the fallback; if the ray finds nothing, the nearest enabled Interactable in the old 0.8 m sensor in front of the view is. set_hovered(true/false) is called on change. LMB/E press: target.press(pid), or for a legacy Interactable interact_pressed.emit(it); with nothing connected to interact_pressed the player calls it.use(self) itself, so `used` fires once either way. hold_seconds > 0: hold_progress, then hold_complete(pid) / interact_held; a release within 0.3 s is a press. An optional pressable var `hand_anim: StringName` (e.g. &"pull") picks the hand animation. Input-off clears hover, cancels a hold and emits primary_released.

fp.summary:
I rebuilt the local player as a first-person controller with mitten hands and a 3D ID card. The game rules, the networking and all public API the director, net code and bots use are unchanged.

**What changed**
- **Head (`CameraRig`, rewritten in place, class name and API kept):**
  - Eye at 1.55 m, mouse look clamped to ±85°, FOV 78 with a small widening while running.
  - Head bob that fires footstep events, a spring dip on landing, and lunges and roll for dives, tackles and tumbles.
  - Carried: the view rides the guard's shoulder looking back and down with a wobble. Detained: hidden, placed by teleport.
- **Your own body:** it still animates and syncs, but sits on a layer your camera skips. Teammates see you; you see only your hands. Remote players get a body and no camera or hands.
- **Pressing:** each physics frame a ray from the screen centre (2.6 m, layer 5) finds what you look at.
  - It hovers and unhovers the target and tells the HUD the hint text.
  - LMB or E presses it; a hold-type target reports progress, then completes; a quick tap counts as a press.
  - A machine can capture LMB for raw press/release, e.g. a dice throw.
- **Legacy tables and stations:** when nothing pressable is in the ray, the nearest legacy station in front of the view is used. That keeps today's director flows working.
- **Hands:** two big toon mitten hands with outlines (3 fingers and a thumb each), built with the art agent's toolkit.
  - Idle sway, walk bob in step with footsteps, lag when you turn.
  - They pull back when you're right against a wall.
  - Animations: press (index finger reaches the button you clicked), point, grab, throw, shake, wave, shove, pull, flip_card and celebrate.
  - They can hold an item in both cupped hands or one palm, and release it where it is.
- **ID card:** a laminated card with an outfit-colour portrait, NAME / BORN / FROM, a grade stamp, a BANKED / CAP bar, a hologram and a FLAGGED or BURNED stamp.
  - Tab raises it in the left hand; the mouse wheel asks the director to swap IDs while it's up.
  - The printed face is flat-coloured so the text stays readable under the club lighting.
- **Sync:** look pitch is now synced too, so remote heads can follow it.

**Tests**
- My two test files pass: 44 tests (22 rewritten player tests, 22 new first-person tests). They cover:
  - camera-relative movement and mouse-look clamps
  - hover and press on a test pressable, holds, capture, E as an alias, input-off
  - the legacy path, hand hold/release keeping world transforms, the finger reaching its target, every animation finishing
  - the ID card, body visibility, puppet pitch and the sync config
- The player-facing integration files (director, net director, progression UI, input setup) pass: 75 tests across six files.
- The autopilot and two-process net tests pass.
- Full suite: 828 passed, 3 failed. All 3 failures are in `test_character_model.gd`: `CharacterModel.get_slot_color` crashes since `Primitives.material` became a shader material. Separately, `test_interactable.gd` logs script errors from the same cause.

**Screenshots** (compatibility renderer under Xvfb; the reference style is matched with original designs):

kit.summary:
The diegetic kit and the GameMachine base are built and tested. My two test files pass (42 tests, no errors). Every visual piece was rendered under Xvfb and checked against the reference images.

**What works**
- **Real-player check.** A test drives an actual first-person `PlayerCharacter` at a machine:
  - Walking into the play spot seats you.
  - The camera ray finds and hovers the keypad keys and the main key.
  - Clicking LMB on SPIN places a bet through the sim.

  So the shared press contract and the player-layer zone work together end to end.
- **Sit / stand.** Walking in requests a sit; walking out requests a stand. If you step into a second machine's spot, leaving the first one does not stand you up. Remote players' bodies and puppets never trigger a sit. A sit refused for a passing reason (e.g. "too far" on a co-op host) is retried every second while you stand there.
- **Occupant-only play.** Occupants are tracked from seated/stood events for every player. Anyone else gets "Occupied" (or "Step up to play") on the console screen, and their key presses are ignored, including typing a bet.
- **Requests and results.** Every request goes through SimHost. The console locks until the request is answered and the result animation finishes. Refusals show a short reason on the screen. Pocket changes wait until the result has played, so the screen never gives away a win or loss early.
- **Fire alarm.** The machine closes: velvet rope with a red CLOSED plaque, console locked. It reopens when the alarm ends, and a machine built during an alarm starts closed.
- **Dealer swap.** With a dealer, a cool-tinted dealer walks in to replace the old one. Without a dealer, the machine flashes cold and pops "COOLED".
- **Generic fallback.** The base class's default behaviour makes every game type playable (bets, high-low runs, blackjack deal/hit/stand), so `MachineFactory` falls back to `TestMachine` for any missing machine script.

**Look**
- The bet console matches the keypad-console and console-on-stand references:
  - Cream keypad with a red C.
  - A screen showing Min/Max, the bet big in yellow, and Pocket.
  - An orange MIN ½ ×2 MAX column with a red THROW toggle that glows while armed.
  - A big green PLAY and fat action keys.
  - A pink neon trim around the panel.
- A hovered key gets a thick yellow glowing ring plus the toon hover outline, and keys sink and spring back when pressed.
- Cards have extruded suit shapes (the font has no suit glyphs) and a purple back with a gold star.
- Dice are pink with glowing pips. Monitors on stands look like the dice-table reference.
- Long floating game names shrink to fit, so neighbouring machines' labels don't overlap.

Screenshots are in the scratchpad `kit/` folder (paths in files): `console_fp.png` and `console_armed.png` (console up close in first-person framing), `kit_row.png`, `kit_cards_dice.png` and `kit_keys_close.png` (the row of kit pieces), and `machine_fp.png`, `machine_round.png` and `machine_closed.png` (the fallback machine in first person and closed). Probe scripts stay in the scratchpad, not the repo.

**Unit suite**
The full unit suite currently has failures in `test_character_model.gd` (68 failing assertions) and one script error in `test_interactable.gd`. They appear to come from the in-place art changes: `CharacterModel` reads `albedo_color` from what is now a toon ShaderMaterial. That is not in my files.

Bots and autopilot can walk to machine.get_play_transform() and use press_by_id or get_aim_point.
